title: Commercial Underwriting Submission Intake
summary: Turn broker emails, proposal forms, schedules of values and loss histories into a structured, checked submission record, with gaps and appetite issues flagged for the underwriter.

seo.title: Commercial Underwriting Submission Intake AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that reads broker submissions, normalises schedules of values and loss histories, checks appetite and completeness, and prepares files for underwriters.

problem.intro: Commercial submissions arrive by email from brokers in every shape: a placement slip, a proposal form, a location schedule in a spreadsheet with merged cells, a risk inspection report and several years of claims experience. Before an underwriter can think about the risk, someone has to key it in, chase what is missing and check whether another broker has already sent the same client.

pain_points.title: Keying before underwriting
pain_points.detail: Underwriting assistants re-enter insured details, sums insured by location and loss history into the workbench, which delays quotes in busy renewal months.

pain_points.title: Messy schedules of values
pain_points.detail: Location schedules mix building, plant and stock values, use different occupancy terms and rarely add up to the sum insured on the proposal form.

pain_points.title: Missing information found late
pain_points.detail: A missing fire NOC, inspection report or claims history is often discovered after the underwriter has started reviewing, so the broker query goes out late.

pain_points.title: Clearance and appetite checks are manual
pain_points.detail: Duplicate submissions from competing brokers and risks outside appetite are spotted from memory, not through a consistent check.

solution.overview: We build an intake agent that watches your underwriting mailbox or broker portal. It reads each email and its attachments, identifies the line of business, the insured and the broker, and extracts the data your underwriting guidelines need. Schedules of values are normalised into a clean location table with occupancy, construction and values split by building, plant and stock, then reconciled to the proposal. Loss histories become a year-by-year summary. The agent checks completeness, clearance and appetite rules, drafts a broker query for gaps and gives the underwriter a summary with every figure linked to its source. Pricing and acceptance stay with the underwriter.
capabilities: Classifies submissions by line of business, such as property, engineering, marine cargo, liability or group health
Extracts insured, broker, period, limits, deductibles and requested covers from slips and proposal forms
Normalises messy schedules of values into a clean location table and reconciles totals to the proposal
Summarises loss history by year, cause and amount, with large losses called out
Runs clearance against existing submissions and policies, and checks appetite and referral rules from your guidelines
Drafts a broker query for missing documents and gives the underwriter a source-linked summary

workflow.title: Capture the submission
workflow.detail: Emails and attachments from the underwriting mailbox or broker portal are grouped into one submission.

workflow.title: Classify and extract
workflow.detail: Line of business, insured, broker and requested cover are identified, and key fields are extracted from each document.

workflow.title: Normalise schedules and losses
workflow.detail: Location schedules and loss histories are converted into standard tables and reconciled to the proposal.

workflow.title: Check clearance, appetite and completeness
workflow.detail: Duplicates, out-of-appetite features and missing documents are flagged against your rules.

workflow.title: Resolve gaps
workflow.detail: An underwriting assistant reviews the flags and sends the drafted broker query where information is missing.

workflow.title: Underwriter review
workflow.detail: The underwriter receives a source-linked summary in the workbench and decides whether and how to quote.

inputs: Broker email, placement slip or market reform contract
Proposal form and expiring policy schedule
Schedule of values or location list in Excel
Loss history or claims experience statement
Employee census for group health submissions
outputs: Structured submission record in the underwriting workbench
Normalised location table with values reconciled to the proposal
Loss history summary by year and cause
Drafted broker query for missing information
Underwriter summary with source-cell and page links
human_in_the_loop: Underwriting assistants review every flag and approve broker queries before they are sent. Underwriters make all decisions on acceptance, terms and price; the agent prepares the file and never quotes.
integrations: Shared underwriting mailbox on Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace
Underwriting workbench or policy administration system
Geocoding and natural hazard data services
guardrails: No pricing, acceptance or declinature by the agent
Appetite and referral rules owned and versioned by underwriting, not inferred by the model
Every extracted figure linked to its source cell or page
Location totals reconciled to the proposal sum insured, with differences flagged
Submissions kept separate by broker so one broker's documents never appear in another broker's file
compliance_notes: Group health census data is personal data under the DPDP Act 2023, so it is masked in logs and access is limited to the underwriting team.
Keeps underwriting authority with authorised underwriters, consistent with the delegated authority structures insurers already maintain.

pilot.scope: Property and fire submissions from one regional underwriting mailbox, processed retrospectively and then in shadow mode for new submissions.
deliverables: Field schema and appetite rules agreed with underwriting
Working intake pipeline on real, access-controlled submissions
Production plan covering further lines of business

faqs.q: Can it handle our brokers' messy spreadsheets?
faqs.a: Yes. It reads multi-tab workbooks, merged cells and inconsistent headings, and maps columns to your location schema. Where a mapping is uncertain, it asks the assistant to confirm rather than guessing.

faqs.q: Does it work with London market or ACORD-style submissions?
faqs.a: Yes. The extraction schemas are configurable, so market reform contracts, ACORD-style forms and Indian proposal formats can each map into one submission record.

faqs.q: Will it price risks or recommend terms?
faqs.a: No. It prepares and checks information. Rating, terms and the decision to quote remain with your underwriters.
Submissions are stored and displayed per broker and per insured, with role-based access. Clearance checks compare identities without exposing one broker's documents to another.
